references.text: The Lord your God will drive out these nations before you little by little. You cannot wipe them out at once, for then the wild animals would become too numerous for you.
Continuation of the promise regarding gradual expulsion, explaining that God will drive out the enemies little by little until Israel has grown and can take possession of the land.
Warning that wild animals will multiply in the land as a consequence of disobedience, illustrating the connection between population density and control over wildlife.
Description of the good land into which the Lord is leading His people, providing context for why gradual conquest was necessary.
Fulfillment of the promise that God drove out the nations, not by sword or bow alone, but through God's own action.
Historical example showing how wild animals (lions) became a problem when the land was depopulated after Israel was exiled and replaced with few inhabitants.
Contrast reference: Explains how God's original plan for gradual conquest turned into a trap due to Israel's disobedience.
